inline.s: [Commentary] Generally the Buddha delivers beings and beings are transformed; within it the difficult and the easy, the shallow and the deep all lie in the affinity. Where the affinity is, the grace and merit are vast and deep; the various teachings awaken and lead beings to joyfully believe and enter, can stir the seeds of their past lives, can make demonic obstacles hard to block, and can open and develop their essential nature. The Buddhas originally come forth from the Dharma-body and firmly bind the seeds of affinity; whether worldly or world-transcending, all of it is inconceivable. Honored within the teachings of the vehicles, raised up within the ocean of the assembly, seeping into the sea of suffering, in compassion joined with the still light — for this reason the myriad virtues revere and receive, and all spirits face toward the Ultimate. One should know that the Buddha-seed arises from conditions, and conditions are the dharma-realm. One thought is all thoughts; one birth is all births. One incense, one flower; one sound, one form — even receiving confession and prophecy, the touch of the hand on the head and the lowered hand — throughout the ten directions and the three times, nothing is not completely fused. Therefore this predominant-condition cause is called the dependent arising of the dharma-realm. This is precisely what is meant by universally contemplating the dharma-realm. Those of shallow capacity can then resolve and seek it exclusively; those of deep capacity need not abandon the West and seek the Avatamsaka elsewhere. If one says the West is provisional and the Avatamsaka is ultimate, the West is small and the Avatamsaka is great, one wholly falls into the clinging of beings’ discriminating imagination, because one does not reach the oneness of the provisional and the ultimate, and the non-inherent nature of great and small.

[Annotation] This makes clear the reason for the three meanings stated above and explains the answer: contemplating and binding the mind to the Western Land of Utmost Bliss is precisely universally contemplating the dharma-realm.
Ding-2, Inquiring and Explaining the Sutra Title

Shariputra! What do you think? Why is it named the Sutra Protected and Remembered by all the Buddhas? Shariputra! If there are good men or good women who hear this sutra and uphold it, and who hear the names of all the Buddhas, these good men and good women are all protected and remembered by all the Buddhas, and all attain non-regression from anuttara-samyak-sambodhi. Therefore, Shariputra! You should all faithfully accept my words and what the Buddhas have spoken.

[Commentary] This sutra exclusively sets forth the supremely essential teaching of the mind and the names of all the Buddhas, and likewise sets forth the supremely perfect, ultimate myriad merits; therefore those who hear it are all protected and remembered by the Buddhas. Moreover, hearing the sutra and upholding it is to hold the name. The name of Amitabha is protected and remembered by all the Buddhas.

[Annotation] This sutra exclusively sets forth the supremely essential teaching of the mind and the names of all the Buddhas, and likewise sets forth the supremely perfect, ultimate myriad merits; therefore those who hear it are all protected and remembered by the Buddhas. Moreover, hearing the sutra and upholding it is to hold the name, and the name of Amitabha Buddha is surely protected and remembered by all the Buddhas.

[Set forth] To explain in detail, to illuminate the facts and the principle. [The names of all the Buddhas] The names of all the Buddhas are precisely the name of Amitabha. Earlier it was said, “Amitabha is the Dharma-body, the treasury of all the dharma-realm; to be mindful of Amitabha, the one Buddha, is to be mindful of all the Buddhas.” Therefore it is said that this sutra exclusively sets forth the names of all the Buddhas.

[Commentary] Question: If one merely hears the names of the Buddhas without having upheld this sutra, does one also receive protection and non-regression? Answer: This meaning has both a restricted and a universal sense. The Sutra of Divining says that a confused and defiled mind, though it recites my name, is not counted as having heard it. Because one cannot give rise to settled faith and understanding, one only obtains worldly good retribution and not the vast, deep, and wonderful benefit; if one reaches the single-practice samadhi, then one accomplishes the vast, subtle, wonderful mind of practice, and is called one who attains the tolerance of non-arising dharmas in resemblance; only then is one counted as having heard the names of the Buddhas of the ten directions. This should likewise be so. Therefore one must, after hearing, hold it until the mind is single and undisturbed, and only then is one counted as having heard the names of all the Buddhas and received the protection and remembrance of all the Buddhas. This is the restricted sense.

[Annotation] [Divining] That is, the Sutra of Divining the Good and Evil Karmic Retribution. [The tolerance of non-arising dharmas] Abbreviated as the tolerance of non-arising. One realizes that all dharmas are illusions, that from the beginning they never arose and so have no cessation (neither arising nor ceasing), and abides in this principle without being moved. “Tolerance” means abiding, that is, the mind abides in the principle without being moved. In the Mahaparinirvana Sutra, Chapter
Kaundinya, the Buddha says: “All dharmas are all false.” In the Great Treatise on the Perfection of Wisdom,

Chapter Fifty, it says: “The tolerance of non-arising dharmas is, within the real character of all dharmas which are neither arising nor ceasing, to believe, receive, and reach through without obstruction and without regression; this is called the tolerance of non-arising.” [This should likewise be so] “This” refers to this sutra, in contrast to that Sutra of Divining the Good and Evil Karmic Retribution; “should likewise be so” means it is likewise the case. This says: the Sutra of Divining speaks of “if one reaches the single-practice samadhi ... only then is one counted as having heard the names of the Buddhas of the ten directions”; this sutra is likewise so — one must, after hearing, hold it until the mind is single and undisturbed, and only then is one counted as having heard the names of all the Buddhas and received the protection and remembrance of all the Buddhas.

[Commentary] As for the universal sense, the compassion of the Buddhas is inconceivable, and the merit of the name is likewise inconceivable. Therefore on merely hearing the Buddha’s name, whether with a mind or without a mind, whether believing or not, one all forms the seed of an affinity. Still more, the Buddha delivers beings without distinguishing enemies from kin, ever without weariness; if one merely hears the Buddha’s name, the Buddha must protect and remember him. How could there be any doubt? Yet according to the Diamond Three Treatises, a bodhisattva whose faculties are matured is protected and remembered by the Buddhas, at the stage of the Distinct Teaching’s stage of the perfect abiding. This is speaking of self-power; one must enter the same-nature [stage] to be protected and remembered. Now relying on the other-power, so even the stage of resemblance receives protection and remembrance. Even down to the resemblance stage and below, all have the meaning of universal protection and remembrance. Down to merely hearing the Buddha’s name, one has the power to nurture and rouse within the same-substance Dharma-nature, and so obtains the distant cause and ultimately does not regress. Anuttara, which is translated as supreme. Samyak-sambodhi, which is translated as right, equal, and true awakening. That is the fruit-awakening of the Mahayana. The perfect three non-regressions is another name for the attainment of Buddhahood in one lifetime. Therefore Shariputra and the others are urged to all faithfully accept it. So great is the merit of hearing the name — spoken alike by Shakyamuni and all the Buddhas of the ten directions — how can one not believe it!

[Annotation] [This is speaking of self-power] This is because, speaking of self-power, [one must enter the same-nature stage]. [The perfect three non-regressions is another name for the attainment of Buddhahood in one lifetime] To perfectly realize the stage of the three non-regressions and to attain Buddhahood in one lifetime are the same in meaning. [Shariputra] The Chinese translation of Shariputra.
[Commentary] First, exhorting faith for circulation, concluded.
[Annotation] Bing-1, exhorting faith for circulation, concludes here.
Bing-2, Exhorting the Vow for Circulation

[Annotation] For ease of understanding the scriptural meaning taught below, that making the vow brings immediate rebirth, the corresponding passage in Master Xuanzang’s translation, the Sutra of the Praise of the Pure Land in Which the Buddha Receives and Upholds, for the preceding sentence (“Therefore, Shariputra! You should all faithfully accept my words and what the Buddhas have spoken.”) is set out:

Therefore, Shariputra! All you beings should faithfully accept and understand the words of me and the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, of the ten directions, and should diligently and earnestly strive, practicing as taught, harboring no doubt.”
Please note the eight characters “diligently and earnestly strive, practicing as taught.”
Question: What is “practicing as taught”?
Answer: It is what the World-Honored One taught above: faith, vow, and holding the name, with a single mind and without disturbance.

Shariputra! If there are people who have already made the vow, or now make the vow, or will make the vow, desiring to be reborn in the land of Amitabha Buddha, these people all attain non-regression from anuttara-samyak-sambodhi; and in that land they are either already born, now born, or will be born. Therefore, Shariputra! If good men and good women have faith, they should make the vow and be reborn in that land.

[Commentary] Already vowed, already born; now vowing, now born; will vow, will be born — this precisely shows that the vow produced in dependence on faith is not empty. Without faith one cannot make the vow; without the vow, faith likewise does not arise. Therefore it is said, if there are those who have faith, they should make the vow.

[Commentary] Moreover, the vow is the warrant of faith and the pivot of practice; it is especially an essential matter. In raising the vow, faith and practice are contained within it, and so it is earnestly urged three times.

[Annotation] [The vow is the warrant of faith and the pivot of practice] A metaphor: when faith has the vow, then the written warrant (contract) is in hand, and there is certainly no repenting; when practice has the vow, then the door-hinge is firmly set, and there is certainly no toppling.

[Commentary] Furthermore, vowing to be reborn in that land is the two gates of longing and turning away. Turning away from the Saha world corresponds to the two great vows produced in dependence on the two truths of suffering and its origin. Longing for the Land of Utmost Bliss corresponds to the two great vows produced in dependence on the two truths of the path and cessation. Therefore one attains non-regression in the great bodhi path.

[Annotation] [The two great vows produced in dependence on the two truths of suffering and its origin] In dependence on the truth of suffering, one produces the vow “beings without limit, I vow to deliver them”; in dependence on the truth of the origin, one produces the vow “afflictions without end, I vow to cut them off.” [The two great vows produced in dependence on the two truths of the path and cessation] In dependence on the truth of the path, one produces the vow “Dharma-doors without measure, I vow to learn them”; in dependence on the truth of cessation, one produces the vow “the Buddha-way supreme, I vow to accomplish it.”

[Commentary] Question: The vow now made can only be spoken of as “will be born,” why is it called “now born”? Answer: This also has two meanings. One, taking one lifetime as “now”: making the vow and holding the name in this present life, at the end of life one is certainly reborn in the Pure Land. Two, taking an instant as “now”: one thought in concordance is one thought of rebirth; thought after thought in concordance is thought after thought of rebirth. The wonderful cause and wonderful fruit do not leave the one mind, like the two ends of a scale, where the rising and falling are equal in time. Why must one wait until the retribution of the Saha world is exhausted before being nurtured in the jewel pond? Just now, by faith, vow, and holding the name, the lotus is bright and beautiful, and the golden platform’s shadow appears — no longer are [such a one] a person within the bounds of the Saha world. Utterly round, utterly sudden, hard to discuss and hard to conceive — only great wisdom can truly believe this.

[Annotation] [Like the two ends of a scale, where the rising and falling are equal in time] Like the two ends of a scale; though the rising and falling differ, they are at the same time and on the same scale. A metaphor that it does not leave the one mind, and is all at a single time.
Bing-3, Exhorting Practice for Circulation:
Ding-1, The Buddhas in Turn Praise; Ding-2, The Teaching-Master’s Concluding Exclamation
Ding-1, The Buddhas in Turn Praise

Shariputra! As I now praise the inconceivable merits of the Buddhas, so these Buddhas likewise praise my inconceivable merits, saying: Shakyamuni Buddha is able to do what is extremely difficult and rare. He is able, in the Saha land, in the evil world of the five defilements — the defilement of the age, the defilement of views, the defilement of afflictions, the defilement of beings, and the defilement of life — to attain anuttara-samyak-sambodhi, and for the sake of all beings to speak this Dharma, hard to believe for all the worlds.

[Commentary] Though the merit and wisdom of all the Buddhas are equal, in the transforming of beings there is difficulty and ease. To accomplish bodhi in the Pure Land is easy; in the defiled world it is difficult. To speak the Dharma for beings of the Pure Land is easy; for beings of the defiled world it is difficult. To speak the gradual Dharma for beings of the defiled world is still easy; to speak the sudden Dharma is difficult. To speak other sudden Dharmas for beings of the defiled world is still easy; to speak the sudden Dharma of the Pure Land’s horizontal transcendence is especially difficult. To speak, for beings of the defiled world, the wondrous contemplation of the Pure Land’s horizontal transcendence, sudden cultivation, and sudden realization is already not easy; to speak of this — needing no toilsome cultivation and realization, merely holding the name, directly ascending to non-regression, the supreme and wonderful, surpassing thought, foremost expedient — is even more the most difficult within the difficult. Therefore the Buddhas of the ten directions all without exception push forth my Shakyamuni as uniquely brave and fierce.
[Annotation] [Toilsome (
qú
)] Toil and hardship.

[Commentary] The defilement of the age is the time when defiled dharmas gather. Within the defilement of the age, without the practice of carrying karma horizontally beyond, one surely cannot cross it. The defilement of views is the five sharp fetters, with wrong views increasing and flourishing: the view of self, the view of extremes, the view of holding to views, the view of holding to precepts, and all wrong views, benighted and submerged, hence called defilement. Within the defilement of views, without the practice that does not rely on expedients, one surely cannot cross it. The defilement of afflictions is the five dull fetters with vexations increasing and flourishing: greed, anger, delusion, pride, and doubt, agitating and disturbing, hence called defilement. Within the defilement of afflictions, without the practice that the ordinary mind is the Buddha-mind, one surely cannot cross it. The defilement of beings is the coarse and defiled union of the five aggregates induced by views and afflictions, provisionally named “beings,” their form and mind both base and inferior, hence called defilement. Within the defilement of beings, without the practice of longing and turning away, one surely cannot cross it. The defilement of life is that its cause and fruit are both inferior and the lifespan short, even not reaching a hundred years, hence called defilement. Within the defilement of life, without the practice that consumes no kalpas and requires no toilsome exertion, one surely cannot cross it.

[Annotation] [The five dull fetters] Five afflictions dull in nature, namely greed, anger, delusion, pride, and doubt. [The practice that the ordinary mind is the Buddha-mind] That is, the practice of mindful recitation of the Buddha. The Contemplation Sutra of Immeasurable Life says: “This mind makes the Buddha; this mind is the Buddha.” [Coarse and defiled] Rough, inferior, and evil. [The union of the five aggregates] The five aggregates are form, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness. Beings take the aggregate of form as the body and the four aggregates of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness as the mind; this is called the union of the five aggregates. [Consumes no kalpas] It is not necessary to spend long periods measured in kalpas.

[Commentary] Furthermore, merely with this faith and vow as the adornment, a single utterance of Amitabha Buddha turns the defilement of the age into the pure ocean assembly, turns the defilement of views into immeasurable light, turns the defilement of afflictions into the still light of eternal calm, turns the defilement of beings into lotus-born transformation, and turns the defilement of life into immeasurable life. Therefore a single utterance of Amitabha Buddha is precisely the Dharma of anuttara-samyak-sambodhi attained by our original teacher Shakyamuni in the evil world of the five defilements. Now bestowing this entire fruit-awakening upon the defiled beings is the realm of practice of all the Buddhas; only the Buddhas and the Buddha can fathom it to the end, not something that the self-power of the nine realms can believe and understand. “All beings” specifically points to the evil men of the five defilements. “All worlds” generally points to the four lands
(the land of common beings and sages dwelling together, the land of expedient remainder, the land of the real retribution of adornment, and the land of the still light of eternal calm)
the world of vessels
(the dependent retribution)
, the nine realms
(excluding the Buddha realm from the ten dharma-realms)
the world of sentient beings
(the direct retribution)

[Annotation] [A single utterance of Amitabha Buddha is precisely the Dharma of anuttara-samyak-sambodhi attained by our original teacher Shakyamuni in the evil world of the five defilements] A single utterance of Amitabha Buddha is precisely the Dharma of Buddhahood (the Dharma of anuttara-samyak-sambodhi) that our original teacher Shakyamuni found for the sake of all beings in the evil world of the five defilements. [“All beings” specifically points to the evil men of the five defilements] “All beings” specifically refers to the people of the evil world of the five defilements.

Question: [Does the statement] “A single utterance of Amitabha Buddha is precisely the Dharma of anuttara-samyak-sambodhi attained by our original teacher Shakyamuni in the evil world of the five defilements” mean it should be understood that the World-Honored One also, in this evil world of the five defilements, recited the name of Amitabha Buddha and thereby realized the Buddha-way?

Answer: Seen from the scriptural text, it should not be understood this way. This sutra says: “Shakyamuni Buddha is able to do what is extremely difficult and rare; he is able, in the Saha land, in the evil world of the five defilements — the defilement of the age, the defilement of views, the defilement of afflictions, the defilement of beings, the defilement of life — to attain anuttara-samyak-sambodhi, and for the sake of all beings to speak this Dharma, hard to believe for all the worlds.” “Shariputra! Know that I, in the evil world of the five defilements, doing this difficult matter, attained anuttara-samyak-sambodhi, and for all the worlds spoke this hard-to-believe Dharma; this is extremely difficult.” The corresponding rendering of Master Xuanzang: “Shakyamuni the Still, Shakyamuni the Dharma King, the Tathagata, the Arhat, the Right and Perfectly Awakened One, the one of clarity and conduct fully perfected, the Well-gone One, the knower of the world, the unsurpassed man, the tamer of men, the teacher of devas and humans, the Buddha, the World-Honored One — he alone is able, in this patient world, in the evil age of the five defilements, that is, the defilement of the age, the defilement of beings, the defilement of afflictions, the defilement of views, and the defilement of life, to attain therein anuttara-samyak-sambodhi. For the sake of conveniently benefiting and bringing bliss to all beings, he speaks this supremely hard-to-believe Dharma of the world.” “Shariputra! Know that I now, in this defiled and patient world, in the evil age of the five defilements, having attained anuttara-samyak-sambodhi, and for the sake of conveniently benefiting and bringing bliss to all beings, speak this supremely hard-to-believe Dharma of the world — this is extremely rare and inconceivable.” All these speak of the World-Honored One, having attained anuttara-samyak-sambodhi, speaking for the sake of beings this hard-to-believe Dharma — the holding of the name of Amitabha.
Ding-2, The Teaching-Master’s Concluding Exclamation

[Commentary] What went before, exhorting faith for circulation, was the entrustment of all the Buddhas; this is the entrustment of our original teacher. The words of the entrustment briefly depart from the particular and follow the general, and merely say “all the worlds,” just as the earlier Buddhas said “you beings.” One should know that Manjushri, Kashyapa, and the like are all within what is entrusted.

[Annotation] What went before, “exhording faith for circulation,” was the entrustment of all the Buddhas; this section is the entrustment of our original teacher Shakyamuni Buddha. The preceding section had both a particular (specific) and a general meaning; in this section the words of the entrustment omit the particular and follow the general meaning, therefore saying “all the worlds” (see the scriptural text below, “for all the worlds spoke this hard-to-believe Dharma”). This “all the worlds” is like the earlier Buddhas’ saying “you beings.” One should know that Manjushri, Kashyapa, and the like are all within what is entrusted.

Shariputra! Know that I, in the evil world of the five defilements, doing this difficult matter, attained anuttara-samyak-sambodhi, and for all the worlds spoke this hard-to-believe Dharma; this is extremely difficult.

[Commentary] The single practice of faith, vow, and holding the name does not involve contrivance and perfectly turns the five defilements. Only faith can enter; it is not a realm reached through thought and discussion. Had our original teacher not entered the evil world, shown the attainment of bodhi, and with great wisdom and great compassion seen this, practiced this, and spoken this, how could beings have received it! Yet when we dwell in the defilement of the age, we are surely bound by the times and pressed by suffering. Dwelling in the defilement of views, we are surely entangled by wrong wisdom and deluded by wrong teachers. Dwelling in the defilement of afflictions, we are surely trapped by greed and stung by evil karma. Dwelling in the defilement of beings, we are surely at ease amid the foul and stinking and cannot penetrate to awakening, content in base weakness and cannot soar. Dwelling in the defilement of life, we are surely swallowed by impermanence — the spark of flint, the flash of lightning — with no time to act. If one does not deeply know its extreme difficulty, one will suppose there is some other Dharma by which to escape the five defilements, and amid the blazing house of the burning mansion the idle arguments flourish. Only by deeply knowing its extreme difficulty will one be willing to put to death the scheming mind and treasure this single practice. This is why our original teacher said at the top of his voice how extremely difficult it is, and earnestly charged us to know it.

[Annotation] [Perfectly turns the five defilements] That is what was said earlier: “merely with this faith and vow as the adornment, a single utterance of Amitabha Buddha turns the defilement of the age into the pure ocean assembly, turns the defilement of views into immeasurable light, turns the defilement of afflictions into the still light of eternal calm, turns the defilement of beings into lotus-born transformation, and turns the defilement of life into immeasurable life.” [Amid the blazing house of the burning mansion, the idle arguments flourish] Within the great burning house, not following the instruction of our original teacher and practicing as taught, one is still there spouting wrong views and idle argument, in a clamorous hubbub. The Lotus Sutra says: “The three realms are without peace, like a burning house.” [Simmering (
fú
)] Rising heat.
